tournament|2025]]) }} '''Emanuel Christopher Sharp''' ({{Langx|he|עמנואל שארפ}}; born March 7, 2004) is a [[college basketball]] player for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] of the [[Big 12 Conference]]. ==Early life and high school== Coming out of high school, Sharp committed to play [[college basketball]] for the [[Houston Cougars men's basketball|Houston Cougars]] over other schools such as Texas Tech, Florida, Louisville, Georgia Tech, Rutgers, Arizona, Clemson, Penn State, SMU and USF.{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=UH picks up commitment from shooting guard Emanuel Sharp |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/UH-picks-up-commitment-from-shooting-guard-16175858.php |website=Houston Chronicle |date=13 May 2021 |access-date=23 March 2025}} ==College career== As a [[freshman]] in 2021–22, Sharp was [[Redshirt (college sports)|redshirted]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |date=February 3, 2025 |title=Why UH coach Kelvin Sampson thinks it's best to rest Emanuel Sharp for two games |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-ankle-injury-20136145.php |access-date=23 March 2025 |website=Houston Chronicle}} As a redshirt freshman in 2022–23, he averaged 5.9 points and 2.2 rebounds in 33 games.{{cite web |title=Emanuel Sharp 2022-23 Game Logs |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/players/emanuel-sharp-1/gamelog/2023 |website=Sports Reference |access-date=23 March 2025}} In the second round of the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]], Sharp led the way with 30 points and seven threes in a win over [[2023–24 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=How Houston's Emanuel Sharp became known as 'Crash' |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/texas-sports-nation/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-duke-19365912.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=23 March 2025}} During the 2023-24 season, he averaged 12.6 points in 37 games.{{cite web |last1=Albergio |first1=Camryn |title=Breaking down Houston men’s basketball 2024-25 roster |url=https://thedailycougar.com/2024/11/04/breaking-down-houston-mens-basketball-2024-25-roster/ |website=The Daily Cougar |access-date=23 March 2025}} On November 22, 2024, Sharp hit five threes in a win over [[2024–25 Hofstra Pride men's basketball team|Hofstra]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=UH's Emanuel Sharp leads the nation in 3-point accuracy thanks to 'confidence' and consistent form |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-3-point-shooting-20030808.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=23 March 2025}} On November 30, he put up 23 points in an overtime loss to [[2024–25 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]]. On January 25, 2025 Sharp scored eight points in a double overtime victory against [[2024–25 Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball team|Kansas]].{{cite web |last1=Ringgold |first1=Buck |title=Kelvin Sampson to hold out Houston guard Emanuel Sharp this week due to injury |url=https://www.si.com/college/houston/basketball/kelvin-sampson-to-hold-out-houston-guard-emanuel-sharp-this-week-due-to-injury-01jk748k5xvj |work=Houston Cougars on SI |publisher=SI.com |access-date=23 March 2025}} On February 18, he notched 17 points with four threes in a victory versus [[2024–25 Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball team|Arizona State]].{{cite web |last1=Duarte |first1=Joseph |title=How UH's Emanuel Sharp went from 'out of whack' to getting his 3-point groove back |url=https://www.houstonchronicle.com/sports/college/article/uh-basketball-emanuel-sharp-rebounds-20175160.php |website=Houston Chronicle |access-date=23 March 2025}} During the [[2025 Big 12 men's basketball tournament]], Sharp helped lead his team to a conference title where he was named the tournament's most outstanding player.{{cite web |last1=Baldwin |first1=Chris |title=Emanuel Sharp Is Finally Feeling Healthy, Lifting NCAA Tournament No. 1 Seed Houston’s Special March Potential Even Higher |url=https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/emanuel-sharp-healthy-one-seed-houston-big-12-tournament-most-outstanding-player/ |website=PaperCity Magazine |access-date=23 March 2025}} In the March Madness tournament, Sharp and the Cougars would reach the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|championship game]], where they fell short at the buzzer against [[2024-25 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]], 65–63. == National team == In 2019, Sharp was a member of the Israeli Under-16 national team and participated in the FIBA U16 European Championship, averaging 25 points per contest.{{Cite web |date=2025-05-01 |title=Emanuel Christopher Sharp (Israel) |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/players/271529-emanuel-christopher-sharp |access-date=2025-05-01 |website=FIBA |language=en}} ==Personal life== He is the son of former Israeli professional basketball player [[Derrick Sharp]].{{cite web |last1=Baldwin |first1=Chris |title=The True Story of Houston’s Two World 6th Man Emanuel Sharp — Pro Player Parents and Israel Smoke Bomb Dodging Give This Freshman an International Edge |url=https://www.papercitymag.com/culture/emanuel-sharp-houston-sixth-man-pro-basketball-dad-derrick-sharp/ |website=PaperCity Magazine |access-date=23 March 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Purks |first1=Scott |title=Blake’s Emanuel Sharp: Charismatic, confident and a beast with the ball |url=https://www.tampabay.com/sports/high-schools/2020/02/07/blakes-emanuel-sharp-charismatic-confident-and-a-beast-with-the-ball/ |website=Tampa Bay Times |access-date=23 March 2025}} Sharp has Israeli, American and Canadian citizenship.{{Cite web |last=Murra |first=Michael |date=2025-02-20 |title=Israeli citizen playing key role in UH men’s basketball success |url=https://jhvonline.com/israeli-citizen-playing-key-role-in-uh-mens-basketball-success-p34561-256.htm |access-date=2025-05-01 |website=Jewish Herald-Voice}} According to [[Sportsnet|Sportsnet.ca]], although being born in Israel, Sharp's "ties to Canada run deep through his mother Justine Ellison Sharp, a Hamilton, Ontario native." His mother played basketball at the [[University of Toronto]] and in 2009 was inducted into the Varsity Blues Hall of Fame. She led Toronto to two national silver medals and was named the women's university athlete of the year in her senior season (1995–96).{{cite web |last1=Sheikh |first1=Zulfi |title=Canadians to watch at March Madness in March |url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/article/canadians-to-watch-at-march-madness-nembhard-swords-fournier-riley-look-to-shine/ |website=Sportsnet.ca}} ==Career
